CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. The injury occurred on Sunday while skiing, approximately 4 days ago. Patient was attempting moguls when her ski strap caught on her finger, causing it to hyperextend or bend backward. She has tried ice and ibuprofen for pain management, but the pain remains severe. Pain is exacerbated with movement.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation, recent. Appendectomy at age 18.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation. Ibuprofen for finger pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Tenderness over distal phalanx of right index finger. Tenderness over the distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Pain with flexion. Full range of motion preserved with ability to bend, extend, and touch thumb with affected finger.

RESULTS
X-rays of right hand index finger: Normal, no fractures, good alignment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion on the tip of the finger. Recommend aluminum foam splint. Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately 1 week. Follow up as needed if symptoms do not improve.
